subject: Streamline Systems — dedicated capacity follow-up: TPS / GPU sizing questions
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + a couple follow-ups from today’s call

Hi Maya — thanks again for the time today. Short recap and two specific asks so we can size a dedicated pool that matches Streamline’s latency and cost goals.

Call recap (high level):
- You’re leaning toward Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) to guarantee throughput and keep inference on private/aws VPC.
- Primary workload: summarization + classification for live chat and nightly batch reruns. Mixed short/long prompts.
- SLA target: 99.9% availability, 95th perc latency ~150–250ms for 8k token requests (typical), lower for short chat.

Actionable asks (can reply inline):
1) Target sustained TPS and expected peak TPS (requests per second). If you have 95th/99th percentiles from your test traffic that’s helpful.
2) Token distribution example: % of requests under 128 tokens, 128–2k tokens, >2k tokens. If you don’t have exact numbers, ballpark is fine.

I’ve attached a lightweight TPS snapshot CSV you can fill (streamline-tps-snapshot.csv) to accelerate sizing.

If Dedicated is the right path, we’ll loop in Ben for a hardware recommendation (A100/H100/L4 tradeoffs) and Vanessa for contract/commit sizing. Proposed next step: technical deep-dive with Ben next week (30–45m) to align on GPU flavor and concurrency model. Are mornings (PDT) or afternoons better?

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee

Date: 2027-04-18T11:44:12-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + a couple follow-ups from today’s call

Thanks Soojin — appreciated the clear recap. Answers below and I attached our token profile for one week of traffic (streamline-map-token-profile.pdf).

1) TPS:
- Sustained: ~12 req/s (we consider this baseline for our 24/7 customer tier)
- Peak: up to ~48 req/s for short spikes tied to product launches (10–15 minute windows)

2) Token distribution (approx):
- <128 tokens: 62%
- 128–2k tokens: 30%
- >2k tokens: 8% (these are batch summarizations that can tolerate slightly higher latency)

Latency expectations: user-facing chat must be <250ms P95 for <1k tokens; longer requests (summaries) can be 300–700ms depending on token count.

Deployment preference: Dedicated capacity inside our AWS account (VPC) — security wants a private control plane + customer-managed keys. Procurement looped in on cc and will follow up with contract and SOC2 questions.

Next step: a technical deep-dive with Ben next week works; mornings PDT are better for our infra folks. If you can propose two slot options (30–45m), we’ll pick one.

Thanks,
Maya

Streamline Systems

Thanks — quick preliminary guidance below (I’ll bring detailed numbers to the deep-dive). This is to unblock procurement with a ballpark.

Short answer (recommendation): H100-based Dedicated pool is the right starting point for their profile if Streamline values P95 latency at 150–250ms on the short tail and needs headroom for 48 TPS peaks. If procurement pushes on cost, we can propose an A100 alternative for the cost-optimized tier with slightly higher latency under peak. L4s are good for low-cost, low-TPS embedding workloads but not this mixed-length generative workload.

Proposed configs (order of magnitude):
- Cost-optimized: 4x A100 (or 8x A100v4 fractional) — supports baseline 12 TPS comfortably, batching to improve long requests; expect P95 for chat ~220–320ms under moderate bursts.
- Balanced: 2x H100 + 4x A100 standby (autoscale/burst) — better headroom for 48 TPS short bursts, lower P95 for <1k token requests ~160–220ms.
- Performance (SLA-forward): 4x H100 with higher reserved GPU concurrency — keeps P95 under 150ms for <1k tokens and faster long-request handling.

Concurrency & batching notes:
- Use small per-request concurrency (1–2 concurrent streams) for chat; enable dynamic batching for mid/long requests.
- Recommend KV-prefix caching for repeated prompts and aggressive batching for >2k token batch jobs (nightly).

Next steps I can take before the deep-dive:
- Produce a short 1-pager with estimated monthly committed cost ranges for the three configs and expected P95 latency numbers (I’ll attach capacity-configs.xlsx).
- Prepare micro-benchmark plan if they want empirical numbers on their token profile.

Ben
